clue.text: Plate sent back for lamb, perhaps

indicators.note: something sent back goes the reverse way, so the word for plate is read from its end

parts.note: a lamina is a thin plate or layer

explanation.surface: A dish is returned to the kitchen because the lamb on it was not right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lamb' looks like the meal on the plate; it is the definition by example, flagged by 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamb is one example of a creature, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Compound of aluminium and potassium and initially lithium

parts.note: Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium
K is the chemical symbol for potassium

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the word that follows is taken

parts.note: the second 'and' supplies its first letter
Li is the chemical symbol for lithium

explanation.surface: A chemistry question asks which substance is made from aluminium, potassium and a touch of lithium.
explanation.walkthrough: The chemical symbols build most of it; 'initially' acts on the second 'and', not on lithium, which gives its full symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: An alkali is a chemical substance, a base that dissolves in water, so it is a kind of compound.

clue.text: Time spent in separating wife from betting income

indicators.note: separating one thing from another takes it away, so the letter for wife is removed
from names the word the wife letter is taken out of

parts.note: winnings are money gained from bets

explanation.surface: A divorce in which a husband keeps his wife away from his gambling profits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time spent in' reads like a prison phrase; in cricket an innings is the time a side or batter spends in to bat.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a batter who is 'in' is batting, and the period of batting is called an innings.

clue.text: Pain in each elbow

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of letters of the next words

parts.note: the letters run on across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone complains of soreness in both elbows.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull continuous pain, a close synonym.

clue.text: Rule about safari initially trapping game creature with big tusks

indicators.note: trapping means the letters for game are held inside the rest
about here means turned round, so the word for rule is read backwards

parts.note: a law is a rule

indicators.note: initially takes just the first letter of safari

parts.note: only its opening letter is used
RU is rugby union, a game

explanation.surface: Safari regulations about catching game, with a tusked animal in view.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of the reversed rule and the first of safari surround RU, rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: The walrus is the Arctic marine mammal known for its long ivory tusks.

clue.text: Likely to listen and open to correction, though losing heart

indicators.note: losing heart means the central letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: something amendable can be corrected or changed

explanation.surface: Someone receptive to criticism, even though they feel discouraged.
explanation.definitionFit: An amenable person is responsive and willing to be persuaded, so they will listen.

clue.text: Perch on back of horse round cowboy exhibition

parts.note: a rod (or perch) is an old measure of length

indicators.note: back of takes the last letter of horse

parts.note: only its final letter is used
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A rider sits on a horse's back at a cowboy show.
explanation.walkthrough: Perch, rod and pole are all names for the same old unit of length, five and a half yards.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a public show of cowboy skills such as bronco riding and roping.

clue.text: Broadcasting vocal number about West Indies

indicators.note: about means the song wraps around the West Indies letters

parts.note: a song is a number that is sung

explanation.surface: A radio station plays a song about the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcasting' suggests radio; it is the old farming sense, scattering seed widely.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasting originally meant scattering seed by hand, which is a way of sowing.

clue.text: Association of blood with pinkish cast

indicators.note: cast means the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, its seven letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: Blood linked to a pinkish tint, as if describing a colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' reads as a tint of colour, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinship is a family relationship, a tie by blood.

clue.text: Simple argument for one getting involved in court case

definitions.text: one getting involved in court case

parts.note: plain means simple or unadorned
a tiff is a minor quarrel

explanation.surface: A straightforward dispute ends with someone being dragged into a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintiff is the party who brings a civil action in court.

clue.text: What Heathrow and Hounslow do to provide with an income

wordplay.note: both place names finish in the letters O and W

explanation.surface: A question about two places near London's airport, and how they might fund someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Heathrow is London's main airport and Hounslow the borough beside it; each name ends in OW, giving END OW.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give a person or institution a permanent source of money.

clue.text: Left tip in advance

parts.note: the tip of something is its end

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a tip before receiving service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' and 'advance' both suggest money; advance is the verb, to lend money.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance money is to lend it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Sweet biscuit a Roman Co. cooked

indicators.note: cooked means the letters are mixed up and made into something new

parts.note: taken as written, these letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: An Italian company bakes a sweet treat.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaroon is a sweet almond or coconut cake-biscuit.

clue.text: Place for judge to sit until bar is represented

indicators.note: represented means presented in another form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, these letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: A judge waits in court until the bar, the legal profession, has counsel present.
explanation.walkthrough: The bar is the body of barristers, which fits the courtroom scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribunal is a court or body set up to hear and judge cases.

clue.text: Murderer of foreigner carrying pounds

indicators.note: carrying means the stranger holds the pound letter inside

parts.note: a stranger is someone from elsewhere
L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A newspaper report of a foreign killer carrying cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A strangler is a killer who throttles the victim.

clue.text: One who has no illusions about a catalogue

parts.note: re means about or concerning
taken as written
a list is a catalogue of items

explanation.surface: Someone unfooled by a catalogue's glossy claims.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist sees things as they are and holds no fanciful hopes.

clue.text: Clever British Conservatives?

parts.note: the right is the political wing of the Conservatives

explanation.surface: A question whether Britain's Tories are clever.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints at the gentle joke of calling Conservatives clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright means intelligent and quick-witted.

clue.text: Salad plant: in haste forgetting it

indicators.note: forgetting means leaving out, so the word it is dropped

parts.note: celerity is swiftness or haste
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook in a hurry leaves something out of a salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Celery is a vegetable whose crisp stalks are often eaten raw in salads.

clue.text: Survivor outside tavern in France, say

indicators.note: outside means the survivor word sits around the tavern word

parts.note: a relic is something surviving from the past
a pub is a tavern

explanation.surface: A lone survivor stands outside an inn somewhere in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In France' looks like a location; the definition is 'France, say', an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: France is a state with an elected president and no monarch, an example of a republic.

clue.text: One of many on board eating river crustacean

indicators.note: eating means the river letter goes inside the chess piece

parts.note: pawns are the most numerous pieces on a chessboard

explanation.surface: A passenger on a crowded boat eats seafood from the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a ship; it is a chessboard, with eight pawns a side.
explanation.definitionFit: A prawn is a small edible shellfish, a type of crustacean.

clue.text: Whiskey needs to mature for financial reward

parts.note: W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to age is to mature over time

explanation.surface: Whisky must be left to mature before it pays off.
explanation.definitionFit: A wage is the regular payment earned for work.

clue.text: Mother's hot brew

parts.note: ma is mother, and the 's carries over

explanation.surface: Mum's hot cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Mash is a mix of grain and hot water in brewing, and in northern England to mash tea is to brew it.
explanation.definitionFit: In brewing, mash is the grain steeped in hot water, a kind of brew.

clue.text: Wheat, perhaps, with resistance in harvest

indicators.note: in places the resistance letter inside the word for harvest

parts.note: to gain is to gather or harvest

explanation.surface: Wheat being harvested despite resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheat is one example of a cereal crop, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Delicate newspaper kept in folder

indicators.note: kept in means the newspaper word is put inside the folder word

parts.note: a file is a folder for papers
rag is a slang word for a low-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: An old, fragile newspaper stored in a folder.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragile means easily broken, a synonym of delicate.

clue.text: Feel prickly and colour slightly about beginning on lie

indicators.note: about means the colour word goes around the letter taken from lie

parts.note: to tinge is to add a slight colour

indicators.note: beginning on takes the first letter of lie

parts.note: only its opening letter is used

explanation.surface: Someone blushes and prickles when starting to tell a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: To tingle is to have a stinging or prickling sensation.

clue.text: Gossipy and spiteful about husband

indicators.note: about means the spiteful word goes round the letter for husband

parts.note: catty means spiteful in talk

explanation.surface: A gossiping person is spiteful about her husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Chatty means fond of light talk, close to gossipy.
